1. Committees Internal Regulations
      This document outlines the internal regulations of Buhurt International Committees. It specifies the
      rules that must be followed by all members of the Committees, regardless of their rank, title, status,
      or other distinctions.

      The document also details the disciplinary sanctions applicable in case of rule violations.


    1.Rules
      All members of the Committee must comply with the following rules:
      1.1.Respect
          Committee members must be polite, respectful, and non-confrontational in all communications
          with third parties.
      1.2.Third parties
          include fighters, team captains, members of Buhurt International Committees, audience, hosts,
          sponsors, media etc.
      1.3.Impartiality
          Committee members must remain impartial and avoid bias toward any fighter or team.
      1.4.Conflict of Interest
          Members of the Committee are prohibited from using their status, rank, title or other distinction
          within Buhurt International to benefit their business or any of their relative’s business (club,
          family, friends etc.)
      1.5.Knowledge
          All committee members must be familiar with their rules and stay updated on any changes.
          Every committee member involved in armors, shields and weapons inspections must adhere
          to the rules as written and evaluate items according to the committee's established methods.
          All committee members must follow the general rules of Buhurt International.




Committees Internal Regulations                                                          3

2. Disciplinary Sanctions
      The committees are responsible for enforcing discipline and ensuring compliance with the
      regulations.
      If a committee member breaks a rule outlined above, the Judiciary committee will issue a sanction.
      An official complaint has to be sent to the Board of Directors of Buhurt International. This has to be
      sent by email: info@buhurtinternational.com.


      2.1.Infraction Classification
      2.1.1. Minor Issue
             A minor issue is a violation of a rule that does not cause damage to the reputation of a
             Committee or Buhurt International.
             It's an issue that isn't severe enough to warrant suspension or removal. However, the
             Committee member must understand that it is significant enough to justify a sanction.
             Examples:
             ●Disrespectful public behavior (including online). I.e: being impolite with third party,
             ●Inadequate knowledge of the rules during a tournament or any Buhurt International event,
             ●Misapplication of rules.

      2.1.2. Serious Issue

             ●   A serious issue is a rule violation that damages the reputation of the Committee or
                 Buhurt International. However, this does not necessarily mean that the Committee
                 member can no longer collaborate with the organization.
             ●   It's an issue severe enough to erode the Council's confidence in the Authenticity
                 Committee member. A three-month suspension is intended to indicate that this behavior
                 is not compliant with the Authenticity Committee's rules.
                 Examples of serious issues:
                  ●Extremely inappropriate public behavior (including online). I.e: insulting a third party,
                  ●Showing bias during armor and weapons checks at a Buhurt International tournament
                   or event,
                  ●Multiple misapplications of rules during more than one event.

      2.1.3. Major Issue

             A major issue is a rule violation that severely damages the reputation of the Committee or
             Buhurt International. This level of breach indicates that it is no longer possible to continue
             collaborating with the Committee member.
             It’s an issue severe enough to warrant ending the collaboration, as it signifies a
             compromise to the integrity of the Committee, making further cooperation impossible.
             Examples of major issues :
                 ●Unacceptable public behavior. I.e: aggressing a third party,
                 ●Multiple sanctions for minor and serious issues.




Committees Internal Regulations                                                          4

2.2.Sanctions

      2.2.1. Warning
             A warning is given by the Council to a Committee member in cases of minor issues.
             It is not recorded nor brought to the Judiciary Committee.


      2.2.2. 3-Month Suspension
             A 3-month suspension is issued by the Judiciary Committee to a committee member in
             cases of multiple minor issues or a serious issue.
             The Council shall notify the Judiciary Committee with all relevant information.


      2.2.3. Permanent Suspension
             Permanent suspension is issued by the Judiciary Committee to a Committee member in
             cases of multiple serious issues or a major issue.
             The Council shall notify the Judiciary Committee with all relevant information.


      2.2.4. Other actions
             In addition to the previous sanction, the Council is allowed to oblige the Committee member
             to improve himself/herself, through mandatory online course, specific trainings etc.

      2.3.Sanctions Protocol

      2.3.1. Council evaluation
             The Council determines the various issues that require discussion during Council meetings.
            Sanctions to be brought to the Judiciary Committee are decided through a vote in a Council
            meeting. The Committee member subject to the sanction will be notified via email of this
            decision.
            The result of the vote, along with any relevant details, must be documented in the minutes
            of the Council meeting.



       2.3.2.Judiciary Committee evaluation
             The Judiciary committee will evaluate the sanction through its own process:
             Please reference “ Judiciary Committee” document
             All sanctions given by the Judiciary Committee will be documented.

       2.3.3.Appeals
             If a Committee member believes that a sanction is unjustified, he/she can form an appeal to
             the Judiciary Committee as stated in their process.
